title: Beef with vegetables without carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens

content.title: About
content.content: Beef with vegetables is a dish where tender pieces of lean beef are simmered with a variety of vegetables, excluding carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens. The recipe does not contain potatoes or tomato‑based sauce, making it lighter and suitable for low‑carb diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is an excellent source of complete protein, providing all essential amino acids.
Stewing meat with vegetables retains most vitamins, especially vitamin C from bell peppers and vitamin A from squash.
Omitting tomato sauce reduces lycopene content but preserves other antioxidants from the vegetables.
The dish can be easily adapted to different cuisines by changing spices and the types of vegetables used.
Slow‑cooked beef becomes more tender and easier to digest.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Beef provides heme iron, which is more readily absorbed and helps maintain healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: High in zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system health and DNA synthesis.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The absence of potatoes and tomato sauce makes the dish suitable for low‑carb eating plans.

items.title: Abundant antioxidants
items.content: Vegetables such as bell pepper and zucchini supply vitamins C and A, which combat free radicals.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Lean beef has less saturated fat, but intake should still be moderated for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Risk of overeating
items.content: The dish can become calorie‑dense due to oil used in cooking; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Adding salt or pre‑made seasonings can raise sodium content, which is a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, pairing the beef pieces with the stewed vegetables. It can be eaten on its own, used as a filling for wraps, or served alongside whole‑grain rice or quinoa for a more filling meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the cooked dish to room temperature, then place it in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat on the stove or in a microwave to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
